h: Getting the best out of your innings
p: If you've never batted against a machine before, don't panic. The trick is to keep your eye on the ball, start with a gentle setting and save the heroics for when you've found your timing. Comfy clothes and trainers are a must, as you'll be shuffling about the crease more than you think, and it's worth leaving the heavy coats with someone who's sitting a round out. A good warm-up stretch saves a few sore shoulders the next morning, too.

For bigger groups, a little organisation goes a long way. Split into teams early, pick a captain who'll keep the batting order moving, and agree a prize for the winners before anyone picks up a bat, even if it's just the losers buying the first round of chips. That way the people who are waiting their turn stay involved rather than drifting off to the bar. It also stops the one serious club cricketer in your group hogging the crease all night.

Bordeaux Quay puts you right in the thick of Bristol's waterfront. Millennium Square and We The Curious, the city's hands-on science centre, are close by, and the M Shed museum sits just across the water on Wapping Wharf, telling the story of Bristol and its people. A harbour ferry trip is a lovely way to hop between spots, or you can stroll along the quayside towards Brunel's SS Great Britain if you've got time to fill before or after your session.
